overview: The red LOS01024T1 Mini-B Brushless makes sense for an aspiring mini racer who has a suitable circuit or an organized class nearby. At 272mm long it is substantially larger than a Micro-B, and the brushless system changes how much usable space matters. Greg Vogel’s RC Driver coverage takes this version to RC Madness and discusses revisions beyond the motor change.
verdict: Buy the brushless Mini-B for a class and a course you can use
verdictText: The documented package makes a strong case for a new mini buggy racer: an assembled car, known power equipment and a chassis with useful tuning resources. Its limitation is the amount of space and class planning that racing still requires.

sections.heading: A miniature race buggy still needs a real place to run.
paragraphs: The red LOS01024T1 Mini-B Brushless makes sense for an aspiring mini racer with a suitable circuit or organized class. At 272mm long, it is a different space commitment from a Micro-B, while the supplied brushless system makes a clear run-out worth planning. Greg Vogel’s RC Driver coverage takes this version to RC Madness and discusses changes beyond the motor. That is attributed outside track work; our recommendation rests on the documented package and does not borrow its laps as our own.

sections.heading: The battery is included; the USB power adapter is still a check.
paragraphs: The factory package includes an 810mAh Smart G2 2S battery, Smart USB-C charger and four AA transmitter cells. Losi’s recorded completion list still calls for a QC 2.0/3.0 USB adapter rated at least 18W. That adapter is the first missing item to check, before buying a second drive pack. A suitably equipped owner can reuse a compliant power source; the presence of a USB socket alone does not establish that an older supply meets the specified charging input.

sections.heading: The 6000Kv system is a complete motor-and-controller decision.
paragraphs: The Spektrum Firma 6000Kv unit combines motor and ESC, while a separate SR315 handles the radio link. That distinction matters when planning changes: choosing another transmitter concerns the receiver’s compatibility, whereas replacing only one half of the integrated motor/controller is a different project. The factory transmission has metal gears and a bevel differential. I would learn the rear-drive buggy with its prescribed 2S pack and stock gearing before paying to change a coordinated power system.

sections.heading: A simple radio can still support useful training.
paragraphs: The SLT2 includes reduced throttle settings so a new mini racer can learn the circuit with less available output. The SR315 receiver also creates a different radio-upgrade path from an integrated ESC/receiver, but compatibility needs checking against the exact transmitter and receiver protocols. RC Driver’s article incorrectly labels the scale 1:18; the official product and manual identify 1/16. That discrepancy does not change the car you should order or justify copying an older brushed Mini-B control description.

For a beginner, the throttle limiter is useful before a transmitter upgrade: it changes how much output is available while retaining the supplied controls. If the planned club has electronics restrictions, resolve them against LOS01024T1 and its separate SR315 before treating another radio as an automatic improvement.

sections.heading: The revisions are reasons to buy the exact generation.
paragraphs: Losi describes a thicker front bulkhead, revised servo saver, shock cartridge spacers and a transmission case that accepts sway bars. These are reasons to identify LOS01024T1 as its own package rather than any Mini-B with a brushless motor fitted. The mid-motor layout, 191mm wheelbase and threaded 7mm oil shocks provide a defined setup to learn. A sway-bar mounting provision is an option to evaluate later; it does not mean the bar is included or required to enjoy the factory buggy.

sections.heading: The stock treads are a starting point for a chosen surface.
paragraphs: Wide Body Rib front tires and Big Shot rears are the recorded factory combination. A buyer choosing a dirt or carpet class should check its tire and motor rules before ordering, because an RTR racing label cannot establish eligibility. For home use, the 272 × 178mm footprint calls for a circuit with gentle jump transitions and room to stop. Uneven grass is a separate obstacle problem; a larger throttle setting cannot change the buggy’s wheel and chassis dimensions.

sections.heading: The aluminum chassis does not replace regular inspection.
paragraphs: The foundation is a 1.5mm 6061-T6 aluminum plate with a screened polycarbonate body. The chassis construction is a fact; surviving a particular impact is not established by the material name. Use the exploded view to understand steering, suspension and transmission access. The stock SX108 metal-gear servo should be checked for free movement and sensible travel before concluding a stronger unit is required. Correcting a mechanical bind should come before adding torque.

The body and exact parts drawing also help distinguish maintenance from conversion. Replacing a worn steering component with its listed part preserves the setup you are learning; changing the servo, radio and suspension together can make it difficult to tell which change solved the original problem.

sections.heading: The complete purchase is close to complete, with one power-source caveat.
paragraphs: The manufacturer price reference recorded on 13 October 2026 was $229.99 for the red Mini-B Brushless. It includes the Smart G2 drive equipment but excludes the specified USB input adapter, tax and delivery. This revision does not establish a current price. There is also a recorded connector-label conflict: the official table says EC2 while the supplied Smart G2 pack is described with IC2 equipment. Check the actual plug and exact manual before spending money on another pack or charging adapter.

sections.heading: The Mini-T trades the buggy format for a shorter truck.
paragraphs: The red LOS-1056T1 Mini-T 2.0 Brushless is the closest complete Losi alternative here. It also supplies an 810mAh Smart G2 2S package and a Spektrum 6000Kv system, but its 160mm wheelbase differs from the Mini-B’s 191mm. Choose according to the class people actually run and the body and wheel format you want. Similar electronics do not prove identical driving behavior. A micro buggy becomes the better alternative only if your available circuit is much smaller.

Both listed packages supplied their 810mAh Smart G2 batteries at the original check, so this comparison is not about one car secretly needing drive power. The relevant distinction is the longer buggy against the shorter stadium truck, plus the format people actually run at your venue.

sections.heading: Buy the brushless Mini-B for a class and a course you can use.
paragraphs: Buy the Mini-B Brushless when there is a usable mini buggy circuit and the supplied power system suits its rules. The package combines an assembled car, drive battery and charger with specific mechanical revisions worth understanding. Its reservations are the additional charging input and the need to settle venue requirements before buying. I would start with the factory gearing, tires and limited throttle, then make one change in response to an observed need. The score assesses this buying package; it does not establish race pace or impact survival.
